Design Thinking for Innovation – Karim Elnazer

Challenge:

During Coronavirus time here in Dubai March 2020, am a father of a family of 4 with my wife and 2  children (13 and 10). As a family we used to go out a lot and we also had very active night life  without the kids. With almost everything closed in the city, as a family we had many ideas on what  we can do during this time we have remote schooling and working from home. All ideas had some  levels of risks (e.g. going out with bicycles or inviting neighbors so increase the possibility of virus  exposure) or investments (e.g. paying for more subscribed TV channels) so needed to prioritize.

Selection:

The tool I selected was Learning Launch to filter and prioritize each idea.

Please watch the video lecture of Bernd Kersten (week 4) for best explanation for the tool.

Application:

I made a family time where I explained to my wife and kids the process. I focused on Data and our  assumptions and confirmation biases. I focused on finding out under what circumstances a certain  idea could be a bad one, and looking for discomforting fact. My son (10y.o.) played a great role in  this being the most skeptic of the family 😊

Insight:

One great insight when we look at the facts that “must be true” was discussing some assumptions  that we will be in this lockdown for only 2 or 3 weeks. Some more pessimistic scenarios can take  more time, so the ideas have to be sustainable.

Approach:

One of things that I could have done differently is to decide to do this regularly, or invite more  friends/neighbors/family via video conference to participate.

propositions.text: The author is a father living in Dubai during March 2020.
The author's family consists of four members: himself, his wife, and two children aged 13 and 10.
The family used to have an active nightlife without the kids before the lockdown.
During the COVID-19 lockdown, the family engaged in remote schooling and working from home.
The family considered activities such as bicycling outside or inviting neighbors but recognized increased virus exposure risks.
They considered investing in additional TV subscriptions to entertain during lockdown.
The family used the Learning Launch tool to prioritize ideas during lockdown.
The ten-year-old son acted as the skeptic in evaluating ideas during family discussions.
Initial assumption was that the lockdown would last only 2 or 3 weeks, which influenced the planning of activities.
During the lockdown, almost everything was closed in the city.
They needed to prioritize the ideas considering risks and investments.
The author selected the tool called Learning Launch to filter and prioritize each idea.
The video lecture of Bernd Kersten (week 4) provides the best explanation of the Learning Launch tool.
He focused on data, assumptions, and confirmation biases in the explanation.
He focused on finding out under what circumstances a certain idea could be a bad one, looking for discomforting facts.
Pessimistic scenarios considered that the lockdown could take more time, so the ideas had to be sustainable.
One approach the author reflected on was that he could have decided to do this process regularly.
Another approach was to invite more friends, neighbors, or family via video conference to participate.

upstream_policies.text: All sensitive financial and budgeting information, including cost payments, feedback on finance procedures, terms of financial facilities, equity negotiations, internal budgeting data, asset accounting details, planning assumptions, project schedules, cost center assignments, corporate pricing strategies, and equity splits, must be classified as confidential. Access to this information is strictly limited to authorized personnel, and employees must not disclose or share such information outside the authorized channels to prevent unauthorized exposure.

All sensitive internal information, including personal, professional, and organizational details, must be kept confidential and accessible only to authorized personnel. Unauthorized disclosure or sharing of such information is prohibited to protect privacy and organizational integrity.

All sensitive financial and transactional information, including repayment details, loan amounts, payment instructions, contract terms, profit sharing, and internal financial adjustments, must be strictly protected and not disclosed to unauthorized individuals to prevent exposure of confidential data.

All employees and contractors must ensure that sensitive information, including technology demos, VR technology usage, device details, technical specifications, tool usage, project testing status, development methods, resource evaluations, product orders, proprietary work, contributor identities, and app service details, is strictly confidential and must not be disclosed or shared without proper authorization.

All employees must ensure that no sensitive or personally identifiable information, including personal, family, financial, professional, or government-related details, is disclosed or accessible without proper authorization. Strict safeguards must be applied to protect such information from exposure.

All employees must refrain from sharing or disclosing any personal lifestyle details, work and social plans, vacation or relocation information, personal projects, and achievements in any public or unsecured communication channels to safeguard sensitive information and maintain privacy.

All sensitive information related to risk management, including risk exposures, operational risks, financial risks, and security assessments, must be strictly protected against unauthorized access and disclosure. Access to such information is limited to authorized personnel only, and sharing outside of approved channels is prohibited to prevent exposure of sensitive data.
All movement details, travel plans, exact locations, times, and related personal or business information must be kept confidential and not disclosed to unauthorized parties.
